title: Data policies (DLP) for Copilot Studio agents
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the control paths, commands, roles and connector mappings. It distinguishes preview endpoint filtering from connector classification and reports the differing documentation for skills, connector blocking and maker guidance.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Copilot Studio guide documents policy creation in Power Platform admin center through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Add an environment > Next > Assign connectors.
claims.quote:
Select Next. The Add an environment page appears.

Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy lists policies for the signed-in administrator's tenant rather than modifying them.
claims.quote:
### Retrieve a list of data policy objects

```powershell
Get-DlpPolicy
```

Gets policy objects for the signed-in admin's tenant.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: The policy creation path continues from Assign connectors through the selected connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints.
claims.quote:
Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector, and then:

Select Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations accepts TenantId, PolicyName and NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations to create endpoint configurations for a policy.

claims.where: summary; What it is; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies govern which connectors apps, flows and agents can use together.
claims.quote: A core component of Power Apps, Power Automate, and Microsoft Copilot Studio is the use of connectors to enumerate, populate, push, and pull data. Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways

claims.where: title; What it is
claims.claim: Microsoft also calls data policies data loss prevention or DLP policies.
claims.quote: replacing legacy data loss prevention (DLP) virtual connectors with modern, environment-level, and environment group-level capabilities.

claims.where: What it is; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: The data groups are Business, Non-Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Connectors in different groups cannot share data, so an app or flow cannot combine SharePoint in Business with Gmail in Non-Business.
claims.quote: if you place SharePoint and Salesforce connectors in the Business group and you place Gmail in the Non-Business group, makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: A Blocked connector cannot be used where its policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Data policy enforcement has been in effect for all tenants since early 2025.
claims.quote: Since early 2025, data policy enforcement is in effect for all tenants, as announced in the message center alert MC973179: Copilot Studio - Upcoming updates to data loss prevention enforcement.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Since March 2025, agents cannot be exempted from data policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Since March 2025, agents can't be exempted from data policy enforcement. It's no longer possible to exempt agents with a PowerShell command.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Copilot Studio capabilities use virtual connectors that are not based on a REST API.
claims.quote:
Virtual connectors are connectors that appear in data policies for administrators to control, but they're not based on a RESTful API.

Microsoft provides several virtual connectors for governing Microsoft Copilot Studio.

claims.where: What it is: connector table, authentication
claims.claim: Blocking Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio prevents publishing agents without authentication.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that don't require authentication, configure a data policy that blocks the connector Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: What it is: connector table, HTTP
claims.claim: Blocking HTTP prevents publishing agents that make HTTP requests.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that make HTTP requests, configure a data policy that blocks the HTTP connector.

claims.quote: | Publishing to Direct Line channels. | Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio |

claims.quote: Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio (applies to the Demo website, custom websites, mobile app, and other Direct Line channels)

claims.where: summary; What it is; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking a Power Platform connector also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on it.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: Blocked connectors and restricted channels appear disabled in the maker experience.
claims.quote: a blocked connector appears disabled when a maker adds tools to an agent, and a restricted channel appears disabled when a maker attempts to add a channel while publishing an agent.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: Makers can hover over a disabled capability for an explanation.
claims.quote: Makers can hover over the unavailable capability to view information about why it's restricted.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: A draft agent violating data policy cannot be published.
claims.quote: When a data policy violation occurs, the Publish button becomes unavailable.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear; Risks and limits: Default group
claims.claim: Published agents violating data policies show DataLossPreventionViolation errors, resolved by updating the policy or agent configuration.
claims.quote:
If your published agent is in violation of your data policies, users of the agent see a DataLossPreventionViolation error when trying to interact with it.

The admin can check the data policy violations and update the policies or the agent configuration as needed.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments covered by the policy scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Add all environments applies the policy across the tenant.
claims.quote: Add all environments: Adds all the environments in your entire tenant. This policy automatically applies to any new environment created in the tenant.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Tenant-level policies can include or exclude selected environments.
claims.quote: Tenant-level policies can be defined to include or exclude specific environments.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Learn says post-2019 connectors such as unauthenticated chat and Direct Line are likely to be in the default Non-business group.
claims.quote: Connectors introduced after 2019, such as Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio or Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio, are likely to be part of the default "Non-business" group.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Learn says that many organisations automatically block connectors in the Non-business group.
claims.quote: In many organizations, connectors in the "Non-business" group are automatically blocked.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that blocking new connectors by default can cause production outages involving Direct Line or unauthenticated website agents.
claims.quote: Misaligned configurations, such as data policies blocking new connectors by default, could result in production outages. For example, essential features like Direct Line or unauthenticated agent deployments on websites might be unexpectedly blocked.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The data-policy documentation states no separate licence requirement specific to data policies at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform data policies DLP licensing cost license required; "data policies" "license" site:learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin. Opened wp-data-loss-prevention, prevent-data-loss and admin-data-loss-prevention; prerequisites name roles, not a separate data-policy licence.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No charge specific to data policies is stated in the data-policy documentation at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "data policies" "charge" "Power Platform"; Power Platform data policies DLP licensing cost license required. Opened wp-data-loss-prevention, prevent-data-loss, admin-data-loss-prevention and connector-endpoint-filtering; no separate data-policy price or meter was stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Class column on Assign connectors indicates whether a connector requires Premium licensing.
claims.quote: | Class | Indicates whether connector usage requires a Premium license or is it included in the Built-in/Standard license for Power Platform. |

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn says connectors requiring licensing not included in the user's licence cannot be seen by that user.
claims.quote: Some connectors require specific licensing, and if your license doesn't include them, you can't see them.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Default group; What to check
claims.claim: New connectors normally enter a policy's designated default group.
claims.quote: You must designate one data group as the default group to automatically classify any new connectors added to Microsoft Power Platform after you create your policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Default group
claims.claim: The initial default group is Non-Business.
claims.quote: Initially, the Non-Business group is the default group for new connectors and all services.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Default group
claims.claim: New nonblockable connectors enter Non-Business even when the policy's default group is Blocked.
claims.quote: If Microsoft adds any new connectors that can't be blocked and you set the default group for the data policy as Blocked, these connectors are automatically marked as Non-Business instead of Blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Default group
claims.claim: A Blocked default group blocks newly introduced blockable connectors.
claims.quote: If the new connector setting is Blocked, any new connectors that are blockable are mapped to Blocked, as expected.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcement takes time
claims.claim: Microsoft documents up to 24 hours for full policy enforcement in the most extreme cases.
claims.quote: For the most extreme cases, the latency for full enforcement is 24 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcement takes time
claims.claim: Microsoft documents full enforcement within an hour in most cases.
claims.quote: In most cases, it's within an hour.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcement takes time
claims.claim: Resources violating a data policy are suspended or quarantined.
claims.quote: If a violation occurs, put the app, flow, or chatbot in to a suspended or quarantine state so that it can't operate.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No channel left; What to check
claims.claim: Agents cannot be published if every channel is blocked.
claims.quote: If all channels for the agent are blocked by data policies, you can't publish your agent.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No channel left; What to check
claims.claim: Agents cannot be published if no allowed channel is configured.
claims.quote: If makers don't configure their agents for a channel that isn't blocked (Direct Line channels are allowed by default), or if the administrators don't allow any channel, agents can't be published.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No channel left; What to check
claims.claim: Direct Line channels are allowed by default.
claims.quote: Direct Line channels are allowed by default

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked; Open questions
claims.claim: Connector classification documentation lists Microsoft Copilot Studio among core connectors that cannot be blocked using data policies.
claims.quote:
The following connectors can't be blocked by using data policies.

| Microsoft 365 Groups Mail (Preview) | Microsoft Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked; What to check
claims.claim: The Assign connectors view has a Blockable column indicating whether a connector can be blocked.
claims.quote: | Blockable | Indicates if the connectors can be blocked or not.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Purview DLP is a different layer
claims.claim: For SharePoint knowledge, Purview DLP at the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents for Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing content with a specified sensitivity label.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Virtual connectors are changing; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft says Copilot Studio virtual connectors are evolving into dedicated governance rules separate from data policies and ACP.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio virtual connectors are evolving into their own dedicated governance rules, separate from both data policies and ACP.

claims.where: Governance controls: custom connector classification
claims.claim: Tenant-level data policies classify custom connectors by Host URL patterns, separately from endpoint filtering.
claims.quote: The Power Platform admin center supports tenant admins in classifying custom connectors by their Host URL endpoints by using a pattern-matching construct for tenant-level data policies.

claims.where: Governance controls: custom connector classification
claims.claim: Environment admins classify custom connectors on the Connectors page in Data Policies.
claims.quote: Environment admins can now find all the custom connectors in their environments alongside prebuilt connectors on the Connectors page in Data Policies. Similar to prebuilt connectors, you can classify custom connectors into Blocked, Business, or Non-Business categories.

claims.where: Governance controls: tenant-wide error message
claims.claim: Set-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings configures an existing tenant error message's contact email and Learn more link.
claims.quote:
Use the Set-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings PowerShell cmdlet to add an email address and a "Learn more" link to the data policy error messages.

To update an existing configuration, use the same PowerShell script, but replace New-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings with Set-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings.

claims.where: Governance controls: tenant-wide error message
claims.claim: The tenant error settings apply to all Power Platform apps in the specified tenant.
claims.quote: These settings apply to all Power Platform apps within the specified tenant.

claims.where: Governance controls: Maker guidelines documentation
claims.claim: The separate preview admin guide calls the Review-pane guidance control Maker guidelines.
claims.quote:
# Configure maker guidelines for Copilot Studio (preview)

The guidance appears in the Copilot Studio Review pane.

claims.where: Governance controls: Maker guidelines documentation
claims.claim: The separate Maker guidelines guide says the feature is available only for managed environments.
claims.quote: Maker guidelines is available only for managed environments.

claims.where: Governance controls: Maker guidelines documentation
claims.claim: The separate Maker guidelines guide uses Edit rule for environment groups in the Copilot area.
claims.quote: Environment group in the Copilot area: Select Copilot > Settings, and then select Maker guidelines. Select the Environment groups tab, select the environment group, and then select Edit rule.

claims.where: Governance controls: sharing limits
claims.claim: Sharing limits are a Managed Environments control over how makers share agents.
claims.quote: You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: Governance controls: sharing limits
claims.claim: Sharing limits apply to agents that require authentication.
claims.quote: Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.

claims.where: Open questions: virtual connector settings carry-over
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether existing virtual connector data policy settings carry over into the new dedicated governance rules.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio virtual connectors transition existing data policies settings carry over governance rules. Read wp-data-loss-prevention, dlp-connector-classification, skills-copilot-studio-rule and the advanced-connector-policies transition search excerpt; no carry-over promise was stated.
